input.quote: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Sections 13.1–13.3 already meet the rule (Affiliates and contractors covered, perpetual irrevocable paid-up licence, revocation only for uncured material breach, transfer to Affiliate/successor). Section 14.2 is the outlier: the Deliverable licence is revocable at Vendor's discretion, non-transferable, limited to the Order Form term, and omits Affiliates and contractors — below the walk-away line for work product created and paid for by us. Redline conforms 14.2 to the Section 13 grant with the minimal edit.

proposal.summary: Conform the Deliverable licence in 14.2 to the Section 13 grant: perpetual and irrevocable, covering Affiliates and contractors, and transferable.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have conformed the Deliverable licence to the grant in Sections 13.2–13.3, so the paid-for Deliverables are licensed perpetually and irrevocably to us, our Affiliates and our contractors, and remain transferable to an Affiliate or successor. A revocable, term-limited, non-transferable licence would leave us unable to keep using work product we paid to have created; if helpful, we can accept coverage of Affiliates on written notice and transfer limited to a successor in an M&A transaction.

ops.oldText: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, reproduce, display, modify, and create derivative works from each Deliverable for their business purposes, transferable to an Affiliate or successor in accordance with Section 13.3.
